name: Atlantic coasts and northern / western inland lakes — format: tools/spots/README.md
Malo-les-Bains (Dunkerque)
notes: Dunkerque Flysurfing Club beach; wide sand flats at low tide, shared with sand yachts and wingers. Local guides say 1 Jul–31 Aug the kite zone shrinks to about 500 m west of the Terminus lifeguard post (prefect's order, text not found: ask the town), the dune zone east towards Leffrinckoucke stays open all year. Short chop in strong wind; offshore and gusty in south wind. Also: Bray-Dunes 12 km east.

name: Les Hemmes de Marck
notes: Very wide gently sloping beach (sand-yacht base on it), flattish water behind sandbanks; best in NW to NE winds, quiet, good for freeride and beginners. Platier d'Oye nature reserve nearby: stay on the beach. Also: Calais – Blériot-Plage 8 km west; Gravelines – Petit-Fort-Philippe 12 km east.

name: Wissant
notes: Between the two capes (venturi): often strong wind and waves, confirmed riders. Wide at low tide, more swell and tougher at high tide; sea-wall rocks and currents. Kite schools on site. In SW wind a downwind run to Sangatte works. Also: Sangatte 10 km north-east.

name: Le Touquet
notes: Kite school Kitezone launches north of the seafront (Saint-Jean 2 car park). Works in SW to N winds; very big tide range, the beach is wide at low tide. The Canche bay works in E winds around high tide (strong currents). In summer the bathing zone is closed to all board sports. Also: Hardelot 14 km north (low-tide pools), Berck-sur-Mer 14 km south (huge beach, flat pools at low tide).

name: Le Crotoy
notes: Tidal bay: rideable around high tide only. Do not cross the yellow buoys: kiting is banned in the Baie de Somme nature reserve (Somme Tourisme; the reserve charter says the same). Local schools are at Cayeux and use Le Crotoy at high tide.

name: Quiberville
notes: Marked kite zone, signposted at the beach entrance: you must stay inside it or kiting can be banned here. Works with W to NW wind (avoid SE to SW offshore). Pebble beach, sand at low tide, tidal currents. Saint-Aubin-sur-Mer next door (school there) is the same stretch.

name: Merville-Franceville
notes: Kite-R Evolution school on the spot. Town order P-2022/003 (art. 12): kiting allowed all year. 1 Jan to 15 Jun and 16 Sep to 31 Dec the whole beach; 16 Jun to 15 Sep only from the Orne estuary to kite channel no. 1 (channels 2 and 3 are closed to kites). It is the only Calvados beach open to kites in summer. NE wind for flat water, NW for experienced riders; best with tide coefficient 70+. Some sites mention a no-launch strip at the far west end (bird reserve): no text found, ask locally. Ouistreham – Riva-Bella is 5 km west.

name: Utah Beach
notes: 12 km of gently sloping sand on the east coast, mainly an easterly-wind spot (flat in offshore W, small waves onshore). Ride around high tide: mussel and oyster beds show up on the beach at low water. No school on the beach (the Jullouville school comes here in east winds).

name: Agon-Coutainville
notes: Wide sand beach by the Coutainville sailing school; the Gouville school brings its students here, all levels. No kite order found: ask the town hall in summer. Also: Gouville-sur-Mer 10 km north.

name: Cherrueix
notes: Bay of Mont-Saint-Michel: huge tidal range, flat shallow water only when the tide covers the flats, so ride around high tide. Works in W to NW and NE winds. Shared with land yachts (char à voile), which use the same beach.

name: Lancieux
notes: Flat, shallow bay with rocks: stay mid-bay and avoid riding alone (south wind blows offshore). Launch point depends on the wind and tide: Tête de Chien for W wind, Rougeret (Saint-Jacut) for N to NE. 1 Jul–31 Aug: Saint-Sieu and Briantais beaches are closed, launch at Tête de Chien (low tide) or Roche Morin (high tide); schools and guides report it, no town order found, so not encoded.

name: Hillion – Bon Abri
notes: Bay of Saint-Brieuc, intermediate level: works in N to NNW wind, ride mid to high tide (the beach is kilometres wide at low tide). The Baie de Saint-Brieuc nature reserve borders the beach: respect its signs and the birds. Plérin – Les Rosaires across the bay works for easterly winds.

name: Saint-Michel-en-Grève (Lieue de Grève)
notes: Huge 4 km sandy beach, no rocks, gentle waves: the easiest place in the area to learn. The sea goes out up to 3 km at low tide (long walk to the water, then a vast flat standing-depth area). Kite's Cool school on the beach (March to November). Saint-Efflam, at the west end, is the same beach.

name: Santec – Le Dossen
notes: Waves; best in S to SW wind, works N to S. In westerlies the inshore water is blocked at high tide: ride low tide. Rocks, all visible. Bathing zone in summer (about 1 June to 15 September, one blog, no town text found): keep clear of swimmers. Green algae in summer at the south river mouth. Kite Sans Frontière teaches here.

name: Keremma
notes: The reference spot of North Finistère: 5 km of beach between the Kernic and Goulven bays, FFVL-labelled and looked after by the Finistère Kite Association. Flat lagoon-like water at low tide (about 500 m of launch space), choppy at high tide. Best in NW wind (NW to NE works). Rocks and a strong current at the river mouth. Dunes are Natura 2000: stay on the paths. The Goulven bird reserve on the west side is closed to all boats. Lifeguards in summer only. Also: Guissény – Le Vougot 10 km west.

name: Pentrez
notes: Long west-facing beach on the Bay of Douarnenez (about 4 km of sand at low tide, 2.5 km at high tide); waves, side-shore in S to SW winds. Kite zone listed by the beach directories; kite school West Gliss in Saint-Nic. Rip currents are reported on the beach.

name: La Torche
notes: Kiters launch north of the point (towards Tronoën), away from the surfers; waves. Intermediate to expert; currents in the water, rocks only near the point. Kite schools at Plomeur (Twentynine, CEKB). Check the beach signs. Also: Tronoën 1.5 km north (kite zone about 300 m south of the car park; current towards the bunker at high tide).

name: Mousterlin
notes: West of the Pointe de Mousterlin; shown as a kite zone on the beach page and in the Brittany tourism board's list of kite spots; an association teaches here. Also: Bénodet – Lagune du Letty 2.5 km west (flat-water lagoon behind the dune spit).

name: Gâvres
notes: Ocean beach (Grande Plage, waves, sideshore in W winds, best around mid tide: shorebreak at high tide) or the flat, shallow Petite Mer de Gâvres from mid tide. Tide decides where you can ride, and part of the area is a military zone: follow the signs. Also: Le Linès 5 km east on the same sandbar; Fort-Bloqué 11 km west (waves).

name: Penthièvre
notes: Bay side of the Penthièvre isthmus (flat water, oyster shells) and ocean side. Ride from 3 h before to 3 h after low tide only. Late May–mid September (29 May–11 Sep in the school and guide sources): bay side banned; on the ocean side take off and land only in the marked zones (north sector, accesses 10–11; Pouladen, posts 1–2, experienced riders). April 2026: the Saint-Pierre-Quiberon mayor said she is considering banning kites on some beaches from summer 2026: check the town hall. Also: Plouharnel – Les Sables Blancs 2 km north on the bay side (NE to SE winds); Erdeven – Kerhillio 8 km north (ocean).

name: Assérac – Pont-Mahé
notes: Shallow bay on the Assérac / Pénestin border, you can stand almost everywhere: the place to learn in Loire-Atlantique. SW to W wind (W is best), thermal breezes. The bay dries out at low tide and the launch area shrinks at high tide, check the tide table. A yellow-buoy zone keeps swimmers apart in summer. Kite school on the beach.

name: La Baule
notes: Plage Benoît and the bay: flat banks at low to mid tide, W to SE wind, choppy at high tide. 15 June to 15 September (period when the channels are buoyed): no kiting from the beach; experienced riders only, through the K13 channel at the Pornichet border (no schools), opened by the lifeguards, wind above 6 knots and enough wet sand (Pornichet order ARR2026-212). Outside that period it is free, at your own risk.

name: Notre-Dame-de-Monts
notes: Wide beach at low tide. Also: Fromentine 7 km north (flat channel facing Noirmoutier, 2 h either side of low tide).

name: La Tranche-sur-Mer
notes: Plage du Phare, facing Île de Ré: waves, wind and current, good level needed, crowded on thermal days. Local guides: May to September the only beach where kiting is allowed (not found in an official text, check the town hall); off season most beaches, but never Belle Henriette. Parking fills up early.

name: Île de Ré – Rivedoux
notes: North beach (bridge to the esplanade), partly reserved for kitesurfing; sheltered from waves, shallow, school on the beach. Works NW to NE (guides). Oyster beds cut the space at low tide, so best from mid to high tide. Stay away from the bridge. Summer limits are set by the town hall: check the buoyed zone.

name: Châtelaillon-Plage
notes: Kite area south of the main beach, in front of the sea wall; two blue flags mark it in summer and it is restricted then (check the town hall). Flat at low tide with rocks offshore, good riding at high tide. School on site. Exposed to swell.

name: Oléron – Plage des Huttes
notes: 5 km beach, windy all year, sheltered from the open ocean; works S to NW and most of all in NW wind (Seulières end). Flat at low tide, shore break at high tide, beach narrows at high tide. A kite zone is set aside in summer (blue flags) and the town hall limits hours: check before riding. Rocks and currents on big tides; schools on the beach.

name: La Palmyre – Bonne Anse
notes: Sheltered shallow bay with a muddy bottom, school on the esplanade. Works in every wind except N and NE. Ride the rising tide, about 2 h either side of high water; strong currents when the bay empties.

name: Lac d'Hourtin-Carcans
notes: Big flat-water lake, launch at Hourtin Port on the east shore. State rules (prefectoral order of 1 Sept 2014): kiting only from 15 November to 31 March, north of the Pointe Blanche – Lacanau channel line, away from the shore strip; the town map shows a kite zone. Check with the schools before a summer session.

name: Lac de Lacanau
notes: Flat, shallow lake with schools at Le Moutchic. Kiting is allowed only in the marked zones either side of the channel to the Talaris marina (prefectoral order of 1 Sept 2014). Also: Lacanau-Océan 7 km west for waves.

country: # archived: no kite channel at Claouey in the State beach rules (Gironde boating guide
region: Feb 2024: only windsurf channels on the basin side of Lège-Cap Ferret)
name: the Cap Ferret kite school has closed
water: no Windy kite marker. Basin spot kept: Le Bétey.

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – Claouey
notes: Tidal basin, 2–3 h either side of high tide; muddy bottom, oyster shells. Closed July–August. Also: Andernos (Le Bétey), La Hume and Les Arbousiers elsewhere on the basin.

name: Lac de Cazaux – Navarrosse
notes: Flat, shallow lake, beginner-friendly; best in W to N winds. Launch from the beach next to Navarrosse harbour, 16 September–14 June only; 15 June–15 September use the Mayotte campsite beach 800 m east (kite school there). Watch the hunting hide to the NE and the harbour channel. Also: Port de l'Estey (Sanguinet) on the same lake.

name: Mimizan
notes: Plage Sud kite zone; keep away from the river mouth currents.

name: Anglet – La Madrague
notes: Waves and a busy surf beach, experienced riders only; stay off the inside where surfers go in and out. Lifeguarded mid-June to mid-September: no kiting during lifeguard hours (10:30–19:00 in July–August, 12:00–18:00 otherwise) or whenever the red flag is up. Local club: Fun Kite Sud Ouest.

name: Lac du Der – Giffaumont
notes: Flat lake, intermediate level. Best with SW to W wind, from March to early September when the lake is full (it is drawn down in winter). Kiting is regulated: ask the KDA club (Arrigny port) before going. Reported: red zone closed 15 June-15 September. Respect the bird zones.

name: Bray-Dunes
notes: Huge flat beach next to the Belgian border; quieter than Dunkerque, regular wind (NW most often); shallow at low tide, more chop at high tide. High season: check the town's beach rules.

name: Leffrinckoucke
notes: Dune beach just east of Malo-les-Bains, the 'batteries' zone that local guides say stays open to kites all year (when Malo is limited in summer). Several wrecks offshore: be careful. Same winds as Malo.

country: # pro: Windy marker (3 stars); kite-forum spot page

name: Zuydcoote
notes: Dune beach between Leffrinckoucke and Bray-Dunes: open sand, regular wind like the rest of the Dunes de Flandre. Dunes are a protected area: use the marked beach access. No school found on the spot.

name: Gravelines – Petit-Fort-Philippe
notes: Wide beach, water shallow almost everywhere (a good place to learn); north dunes side is the kite and sand-yacht area. Town order (2024): kites are banned in the supervised bathing zone, and elsewhere only from 100 m east of it; lifeguards 1 Jul–1 Sep, 10:30–18:30. Big tide range: more space at low tide.

name: Calais – Blériot-Plage
notes: Decent freeride in west winds at low tide, waves in NE storms from mid-tide; launch near the jetty. Ferry traffic nearby, busy swimming zone in summer, wooden groynes at high tide. Thin kite sources: check locally.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 10 km from Wissant

name: Sangatte
notes: Windiest spot of the Côte d'Opale (often over 30 knots, strong gusts): confirmed riders only. Breakwaters on the beach are a hazard. Kite school on site.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 12 km from Wissant

name: Wimereux – Pointe aux Oies
notes: Main launch between Wimereux and Ambleteuse: big beach, dunes to rig, SW to N winds via W. Rocks at the point and along the beach; NE to E is offshore and dangerous. Beach is narrow at high tide. Wimkite school uses it. The town beach of Wimereux works at low tide only (about 3 h either side). One guide reports no kiting before 19:00 in July–August, not confirmed by an official text.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — school beach near Boulogne

name: Le Portel
notes: Kite school APG (Association Porteloise de Glisse) at the beach. Tidal, best from mid to high tide. In N to NE winds the water is flat; in SW wind of force 6+ it is choppy next to the harbour, confirmed riders only. Keep 60 m from Fort de l'Heurt and 100 m from the Digue Carnot in SW to W winds. Boat traffic from Boulogne.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 14 km from Le Touquet

name: Hardelot
notes: Flat water in the low-tide pools and waves outside. Take off south of the channel, avoid the rocks along it (worst at high tide); the FFVL sheet says not to cross the channel in summer. Bathing zone on the right facing the sea is closed to kites. Best in SW to W winds; NE and E are offshore. Kite schools KiteZone 62, Shaka Kite School and Kitecamp62.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 14 km from Le Touquet

name: Berck-sur-Mer
notes: Huge beach; flat pools at low tide. In summer a kite zone of about 400 m between two flagged posts, other beach users have priority (FFVL sheet, no decree found). SW to NW winds are good, NE to SE are bad. At high tide 300 to 400 m of sand separates the sea from the dike. Kite school Opale Kite on the beach since 2011.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — school zone between Berck and the Somme bay

name: Fort-Mahon-Plage
notes: Kite zone north of the nautical-base dike, on the unsupervised north beach. WSW to NW winds, the dunes speed the wind up: intermediate level. Kite school MSKite (EFK) faces the sailing club. Kiting is not allowed in the Baie de Somme nature reserve to the south.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — Somme bay cluster

name: Cayeux-sur-Mer – La Mollière
notes: Between Cayeux and Le Hourdel, on the sea side of the bay. Schools Kitesurf Baie de Somme and Kite Passion are in Cayeux and use this side around low tide (about 2 h either side); at high tide it is a pebble beach. Guides say the stretch in front of the main entrance of the chemin des planches is closed to kites in summer (no decree found). Kiting is banned in the Baie de Somme nature reserve.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — urban pebble beach

name: Le Havre
notes: Urban pebble beach. Main launch is below the Le Ponant building (LH Kite association); stay clear of bathers. Launching on pebbles is awkward and the water is choppy at high tide. Schools in town (Max Kite School, École havraise de kitesurf). Works in SW to NW wind. Town hall rule not found: check signs.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 5 km from Merville-Franceville

name: Ouistreham – Riva-Bella
notes: Low tide only: at high tide the water reaches the sea wall and the wind is disturbed. Best with NE (Orne estuary funnel) or NW wind; avoid south (offshore). La Clinique de la Planche school works from the Ouistreham nautical centre, ride 2 h either side of low water. Stay away from the wall and houses; summer: respect the bathing zones.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — secondary Calvados beach

name: Houlgate
notes: Kite Paradise school on the beach. At low tide the beach forms sheltered pools, good for learners. Intermediate level, NE to NW wind. Summer: Calvados beaches are closed to kites in the day and reopen after 18:00 (check with the lifeguard post). Dives estuary is next to it.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — secondary Calvados beach

name: Asnelles
notes: Wide sand beach, flat water at best. Slalom riding around the Mulberry harbour remains off Arromanches. No school found. Tide coefficient 70+ is advised. Summer: Calvados beaches are closed to kites in the day and reopen after 18:00 (check with the lifeguard post).

name: Colleville-Montgomery
notes: Wide dune beach, little traffic, beginner friendly, best at low tide. Wind NW to SW side-on (guides vary: NW and NE also listed). Equipment rental at OCEAN Espace Glisse. 2 km west of Ouistreham – Riva-Bella. Summer: the busy bathing zones are closed to kites in the day.

name: Langrune-sur-Mer
notes: Voiles de Nacre sailing club (kitesurf lessons, AFKite licence needed). North-facing beach, NE to NNW wind, intermediate level, tide matters (check times). Summer: bathing zones closed to kites in the day (check the town).

name: Courseulles-sur-Mer
notes: Sailing school of Courseulles gives lessons. Side-on NW to W wind, tide coefficient 70+ advised. Summer: bathing zones closed to kites in the day (check the town).

name: Ver-sur-Mer
notes: Weakly sourced (one kite directory line: chop and small waves, no school found). Summer: bathing zones closed to kites in the day (check the town).

name: Deauville
notes: Wide sand beach. In summer the supervised swimming zone is closed to kites and the beach is busy; kite zone is elsewhere on the beach, parking near rue Chauvelot. Open all year otherwise, busiest April to September. Trouville across the Touques is the same water.

name: Fécamp
notes: Pebble beach in town. Kite site listed by the town directory as open in season only: check the rules. Intermediate level, NW wind.

name: Saint-Valery-en-Caux
notes: Pebble beach, shallow and choppy water, beginner level per directories; the beach is listed as a kite site. Check the town rules in summer.

name: Pourville-sur-Mer
notes: Short beach below cliffs, launch and recovery tricky, high tide especially: experienced riders. Best in NW wind (waves), poor in south offshore.

name: Dieppe
notes: Town pebble beach, north-facing, several wind directions, intermediate level. The town directory lists the kite site as open in season only: check the rules before going.

name: Antifer
notes: Tidal spot under the cliffs next to an oil terminal (restricted waters). Works best in SSW to SW wind with some swell; wind stronger and more turbulent than at Le Havre, few usable directions. Not for beginners.

name: Cherbourg – Collignon
notes: Flat water inside the Cherbourg breakwater, around high tide; works W to NE (a strong NE thermal draws the crowd; S wind is side-offshore, avoid). Stones on the left at low tide and a current at the river mouth.

name: Urville-Nacqueville
notes: Home of the Pôle Nautique de la Hague, the only kite school in the Cotentin (lessons and rental, in the old fort). Check the tide and the local rules with the school.

name: Siouville-Hague
notes: Wave spot, all tides, experienced riders. Best wave-riding spot in Normandy; the Hague school (Pôle Nautique) gives lessons here.

name: Gouville-sur-Mer
notes: Beach opposite the campsite, open and shallow, good for beginners; base of the Pôle Kitesurf Normandie school. Not the Cabines de bains beach (oyster parks).

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Granville beach

name: Jullouville
notes: Wide open 2 km beach, flat shallow water, small summer thermal; main W-wind spot of the Fifty Kite school at medium and big tides (Kairon-plage on small tides). Best from mid to low tide.

name: Vauville
notes: Big dune bay (dunes are a nature reserve: carry the gear over them, respect the rules). Works in S, NW and NE summer thermal winds; big shorebreak at high tide, so wait for the tide to turn. Waves less clean than Siouville. The Hague school gives lessons here.

name: Sciotot
notes: Named with Siouville and Urville as one of the known kite beaches of the Manche. Option in SE wind. Check tide and rules locally.

name: Barneville-Carteret
notes: Barneville beach next to Carteret: NW wind comes cross-shore from the right, waves best about 1 h after high tide, rocks show at low tide and the water is chopped at the breakwater (S current). The town's water-sports centre runs courses.

name: Anneville-sur-Mer
notes: Beach used by the mobile Pôle Kitesurf Normandie school when the wind and tide suit; wide, open and stone-free. One school source only.

name: Jonville (Réville)
notes: Beach of Jonville listed by the Barfleur tourist guide for kitesurf, kayak and windsurf. One tourist-guide source and no school: check tide and wind locally.

Most of the beach is covered at high spring tides.

name: Saint-Lunaire – Longchamp
notes: Kitesurf is banned on all four beaches of Saint-Lunaire from 10:00 to 20:00, 15 June to 15 September (town hall, beaches page). Outside those hours and dates it is a known Emerald Coast spot.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Côtes-d'Armor beach

name: Sables-d'Or-les-Pins
notes: Wide sandy beach sheltered from west swell by Cap Fréhel. Best in NE wind (the Erquy school gives lessons here then); NW wind is irregular. Ride mid tide to low tide for steadier wind. Summer bathers: leave the 300 m band through the channel and check the town's rules.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Côtes-d'Armor beach

name: Erquy – Caroual
notes: Kite zone on the west half of the beach only: the half next to the village is a supervised swimming area, no launching. Needs WSW or more for steady wind; at high tide the Pointe de Pléneuf makes it gusty, so mid to low tide is better. Intermediate level, shared with land yachts and swimmers.

name: Plérin – Les Rosaires
notes: Fallback for easterly winds (also N, NE and NW work) in the Bay of Saint-Brieuc. About 2 km of sand, choppy water, gusty in places, intermediate level. Strong tides and currents near the channels; stay clear of the supervised swimming zone in summer.

name: Saint-Cast – Grande Plage
notes: Preferred spot of the Emerald Coast schools when the wind turns east. Summer: kiting before 10:00 and after 19:30 and only below mid-tide, 15 Jun–15 Sep, per a school regulation page (no town order found, so not encoded); check with the town hall.

name: Saint-Jacut – Le Rougeret
notes: North side of the Lancieux bay, for N to NE winds; watch the cliff and shorebreak at high tide. In July and August, school pages say kiting from the Saint-Jacut beaches is banned at high tide; no town order found, so not encoded.

name: Étables – Les Godelins
notes: Flat water at low tide behind a sandbank, rocks on both sides. Works in N to NE wind; careful with mussel shells and with the tide. Kite school O-Rider'School works at Binic-Étables.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 10 km from Keremma

name: Guissény – Le Vougot
notes: Big west-facing beach, no school on site. Thermal wind stronger than at Le Dossen, waves build at high tide but stay easy. Many stones in the water and a shorebreak at high tide. A kite zone is listed on the beach.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Abers beach

name: Landéda – Sainte-Marguerite
notes: Sheltered bay behind the dunes, flat water; works S to NNE, best W to NNW. Sources disagree on the tide (flat at low tide vs. enough water only around high tide): check the tide before rigging. Strong current as the bay empties on big tides, reefs. Summer bathing zone in the south part, 1 July to 30 August (one blog, no town text found). Landéda school AvelWest.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Abers beach

name: Lampaul-Ploudalmézeau – Trois Moutons
notes: Tréompan dunes, one of the windiest beaches of the coast. Best in W to NW wind with waves: higher water, better waves. Long walk to the water at low tide, beach narrow at high tide. Marked kite zones to the left of the beach in July and August.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Iroise beach

name: Le Conquet – Blancs Sablons
notes: West-facing beach under cliffs, catches swell: not for beginners. Wind SW to N, best W to NNW (summer NE thermals suit freeride). Best at mid tide: huge shorebreak and gusty wind close inshore at high tide, waves close out at low tide. Swimming zone on the west part 1 July to 31 August (one blog, no town text found).

name: Brest – Moulin Blanc
notes: Flat water in the Rade de Brest, gusty; best in strong SW wind (onshore). Popular city spot. A spot guide mentions a kite channel in summer. We keep the old closure (1 July–31 August 09:00–19:00) until a Brest text confirms what is allowed.

name: Primel-Trégastel
notes: Experienced kiters only: the guide says best in NE wind (offshore on this west-facing beach), rocks on both sides and some under water, most dangerous towards low tide. Moderate waves, enough for freeride.

name: Crozon – Goulien
notes: Waves; main kite beach of the Crozon peninsula. Crescent beach of the Anse de Dinan, less exposed to swell than La Palue, so riders come here in strong wind or big swell. NE is the wave-kite wind; avoid W wind with a big swell; at low tide you slalom between rocks. Also: Kersiguénou in the middle of the crescent, for S winds.

name: Île-Tudy
notes: Plage du Sillon: at low tide rocks in the middle of the beach make a shallow lagoon you can stand in; strong S winds at high tide give waves and shorebreak. Works E to SW. Crowded with sunbathers in summer; the beach is lifeguarded 1 July–31 August, 13:00–19:00. A midday summer kite ban is reported but no official text was found: check the signs or the town hall.

name: Bénodet – Lagune du Letty
notes: Flat-water lagoon (Mer Blanche) behind the dune spit; riders launch at the slipway below the UCPA. Works only in southerly winds and only around high tide (the lagoon dries out at low water, strong tidal currents): go with a local instructor the first time. Plenty of room beyond the sandbar. Natura 2000 site.

country: # pro: added from Windy (4 Nov rule)

name: Crozon – Kersiguénou
notes: Middle of the Anse de Dinan crescent, 1 km from Goulien: riders move here (or to Kerloc'h in the north) when the wind turns south. More sheltered from swell than La Palue, so a fallback in strong wind or swell. Waves; rocks at low tide.

name: Crozon – Morgat
notes: Sheltered beach of Morgat bay, in the lee of the cliffs; listed with a kite zone by the beach directory. Very busy with swimmers in summer: check the signs and the lifeguard flags.

name: Plonévez-Porzay – Kervel
notes: Wide, flat beach on the east side of the Bay of Douarnenez, listed as a kite zone. Best in southerly winds (cliffs to the north make other winds gusty); often freeride only, waves cleaner than at Pentrez. Campsite holidaymakers fill the beach in summer.

name: Pouldreuzic – Penhors
notes: Long sandy beach of the Bay of Audierne with a nautical centre on the beach; listed as a kite zone, and the sand-yacht school Plein Ouest rents kite gear. Known mostly for surf: waves and rip currents, check the flags.

name: Plouhinec – Mesperleuc'h
notes: Beach used by kiters and freeriders on flat days; with swell it is a mushy beach break. Lots of room and, according to the kite guide, no restrictions.

name: Le Ster
notes: Wide south-facing sandy beach (almost 4 km) facing the Étocs islets; beginners and bump-and-jump riders. W to SW winds are cross-shore. Reef on the right, shallow at low tide. The kite guide says kiting is banned in the daytime during summer thermal winds: no official text found, check the signs.

name: Trégunc – Kersidan
notes: Croissant-shaped sandy beach, a fallback when the west-coast swell is too heavy; intermediate to expert, small shorebreak around high water. The kite guide says kiting is banned in high summer: no official text found, check the signs. Grass to rig on, parking.

name: Fort-Bloqué
notes: Long beach (1.5–2 km) open to the south-west, waves; kiters share it with surfers (surf school at the Pen er Malo car park), busy in good wind. Lifeguards in July and August; check the beach flags. Guidel kite rules: see the Lorient tourist office.

name: Erdeven – Kerhillio
notes: Reference spot of the area (schools on the beach: Rêve de Glisse, You Kite). Ride from 3 h before to 3 h after low tide. Tourist office: kite zone in the south-east part of the beach, beyond the yellow buoys, marked all year. In high season the zone is the east sector (posts 27–28): take off and land only, then go beyond 300 m; at high tide it is discouraged and not allowed from 3 h before to 3 h after high water at coefficients above 85.

name: Plouharnel – Les Sables Blancs
notes: Bay side of the Quiberon isthmus for NE to SE winds; wide beach, the only unrestricted kite spot of the bay according to the guides. Best at low to mid tide, choppy higher up (the little La Piscine bay to the north only works at high tide). Avoid the oyster parks (poles, yellow buoys ~500 m out); wear booties.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Rhuys beach

name: Sarzeau – Penvins
notes: Reference kite spot of the Morbihan: big open area, schools on site (labelled FFVL). Best around low tide; avoid the last 2 h of the rising tide (shorebreak). W to NW winds are offshore here: schools use a safety boat. Currents from the Vilaine estuary nearby.

name: La Trinité-sur-Mer – Men Du
notes: Sheltered bay (about 800 x 500 m) on the Carnac / La Trinité border, mainly for northerly winds. Enough water from mid tide up; at low tide it dries out and the take-off area gets small. Schools of Carnac teach here in summer, when Carnac itself is closed to kites.

name: Larmor-Plage – Kerguelen
notes: Beach of the Kerguelen nautical centre, open to the Atlantic; wind and waves. Shown as a kite beach by the Lorient tourist office; school: French Foil (Larmor-Plage).

name: Gâvres – Le Linès
notes: Ocean beach at the south end of the Gâvres sandbar (Plouhinec side), W winds. Listed by the kite guide with La Caserne and the other Gâvres spots. Waves are moderate; the area is partly military: follow the signs.

name: La Turballe – Pen Bron
notes: Ocean side north of the Croisic roadstead: freeride and bump-and-jump, strong shore break at high tide, little beach left at high tide (sea wall). One guide says kiting is strictly banned here in summer: no official text found, check the town hall before going. Conservatoire du littoral and Natura 2000 land, naturist beach. No kite school.

name: Larmor-Plage – Toulhars
notes: Town beach of Larmor-Plage, one of the few freeride spots of the area; NE wind is a little gusty but side-shore (kite-and-windsurfing-guide). The Lorient tourist office promotes kitesurf at Larmor-Plage. No school on this beach. Also: Kerguelen beach 1 km away.

name: Carnac – Grande Plage
notes: Carnac-Plage beach, home of the Carnac Evasion kite school (FFVL, all year). Summer rule: a guide says kiting is banned in the whole commune in summer except for school members; no town order found, so check with the school or the town hall before riding in June–September. Also: Men Du 1.6 km east.

name: Carnac – Saint-Colomban
notes: West end of Carnac beach and a meeting point for kitesurfers (Brittany tourism board). Guides disagree on the wind: W to SW, maybe NW. Same summer-rule warning as Carnac Grande Plage: check before riding in June–September.

name: Plouharnel – Mané Guen
notes: Ocean side of the Quiberon isthmus, facing west; used by kitesurfers, beginners to experienced, and by wave riders (spot guides). Swell and shore break. Also: Les Sables Blancs 2 km away on the bay side for flat water.

name: Plouharnel – Sainte-Barbe
notes: Large fine-sand beach north of Mané Guen, easy for beginners (spot guide); open to the ocean, so swell. Also: Kerhillio 2 km north (schools on the beach).

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local beach

name: Saint-Brevin-les-Pins
notes: Plage des Rochelets is the official kite beach, open all year; the Ermitage is the wave side. Summer: kiting only in the signposted zone, check the town hall for dates (guides disagree). Schools: H2AIR at the Pointeau, Kite A.Traction at the Ermitage, Line Up (Val d'Or).

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 7 km from Notre-Dame-de-Monts

name: Fromentine
notes: La Grande Côte, ocean side of Fromentine: sandbanks and shallow lagoons (about 1 m) at low tide, no rocks, good for beginners and freestyle; best N to SE wind, 2 h either side of low tide; shore break at high tide with strong wind. Never kite in the port exit channel (ferries). Guides give a 15 May to 15 September ban for the Fromentine beaches: no official text found, check the town halls. Fromentine Kite school at the sailing-school car park.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Vendée beach

name: Bretignolles-sur-Mer
notes: Plage des Dunes: kite zone on the south part of the beach (Dunes 2 lifeguard post), buoyed in July and August. School Bréti-Kiteschool teaches there. Waves and a side current are common.

name: Pornichet
notes: Plage des Libraires, next to the K13 kite channel at the La Baule border. W to NW wind, any tide, shore break, shared with wing and surf riders. 15 June to 15 September: kiting only beyond the 300 m swimming strip and only through K13 while it is buoyed, experienced riders only, closed to schools (town hall order ARR2026-212). Outside that period it is free, at your own risk.

name: Mesquer – Sorlock
notes: Quiet beach near the Pointe de Merquel, much less crowded than Pont-Mahé. One guide rates it for N to NE wind, only the first 50 m gusty: check the wind direction against the beach before launching. A few rocks at low tide. No kite school, one source only.

name: Saint-Brevin – Le Pointeau
notes: Flat riding in a large shallow lagoon in front of a wide white-sand beach, next to the Rochelets. H2AIR kite school at the Pointeau nautical base (March to November). In summer ride in the signposted zone, check the town hall.

name: Saint-Michel-Chef-Chef – Tharon
notes: Glisse Academy kite school has a reserved practice area here (Pornic tourist office). No wind or tide details found: ask the school for the zone and the best wind.

name: La Bernerie-en-Retz – Grande Plage
notes: Beach directory lists a kite zone on the Grande Plage (left side, lifeguarded in season); rocks uncovered at low tide. Glisse Academy and the sailing club work from here. Only tourist sources: ask the school for the wind and the zone.

name: Saint-Jean-de-Monts – Estacade
notes: Base nautique on the Estacade beach teaches kitesurf with a supervised navigation zone; respect the zone and wear a life jacket. Lifeguards 1 July to 31 August. One source only: ask the base for the rules and best wind.

name: Saint-Hilaire-de-Riez – Les Becs
notes: Kite zone south of the Salins beach, between Les Salins and Les Becs (tourist office). Do not launch from the Salins naturist beach, which has a lifeguard post in summer. Kite school nearby (Saint Gilles Kite School, FFVL). No official text found, check the town hall.

name: Les Sables-d'Olonne – Grande Plage
notes: Urban spot east of the harbour mouth. Waves line up at the jetty at low tide; at high tide it gets very tight and gusty near the promenade. Ocean Players kite school on the Grande Plage. A guide says the kite zone is free off season and buoyed in July and August: check the town beach rules.

name: Le Veillon
notes: River-mouth beach with two sides: waves on the ocean side, flat water on the Payré estuary side, where the local school (Ocean Players) teaches. Estuary side best around high tide; the small lagoon dries out at low tide. Reefs. In summer launch only at the end of the beach, swimmers and the surf school have priority; 5 to 10 min walk from the car park.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — second Île de Ré spot

name: Île de Ré – Les Portes (Trousse-Chemise)
notes: Flat water on the sandbank (Banc du Bucheron) that shows at low tide; works E, NE and N, blowing you back to the beach. Confirmed riders: strong current along the bank towards the Fier d'Ars, check the tide first. Club and travelling school on site.

name: La Rochelle – Aytré
notes: Long beach with muddy shallow water, shells and mussels (wear shoes). Ride about 2 h either side of high tide; works SW to NW. Crowded on windy days, school on site.

name: Oléron – Plaisance
notes: Calm, shallow water, no swell or rocks (mussels: wear shoes); good for learning. Works N to NE, and morning SE; any tide. In summer the allowed zone is on the left of the beach and kiting is only before the lifeguards open (11:00) and after 19:00: check the town hall.

country: # pro: restricted (club / permit / summer ban) — banned in summer; Oléron cluster

name: Oléron – La Perroche
notes: Intermediate to expert: SW to W wind, hard to ride downwind, big shore break at high tide. Reported banned in summer (with La Rémigeasse next door; town orders since 2022): no official text found, check the town hall. Rémigeasse beach is being rebuilt in 2026.

name: Oléron – Gatseau
notes: South-facing bay at the tip of the island, flat around high tide. Hard to reach (small train from Saint-Trojan), no school. Strong tidal currents near the Maumusson pass: local knowledge needed.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local estuary beach

name: Le Verdon – La Chambrette
notes: Estuary beach for E to NE winds, 2 h either side of high tide.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — Lac de Lacanau kept; summer restrictions

name: Lacanau-Océan
notes: Ocean beach break, experienced riders; strong currents (baïnes). Kite at Super Sud, away from the surf and bathing zones; summer rules are set by the town each year.

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – Andernos (Le Bétey)
notes: Shallow tidal basin, ride 3 h either side of high tide; sandbank to stand on at low water. In summer kites may only cross the 300 m strip through the marked Andernos kite channel; treated as closed in July–August. Also: La Hume and Les Arbousiers on the south shore.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — Arcachon basin cluster

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – Les Arbousiers
notes: Sandbank with footing at low tide (beginners), current and chop over moorings at high tide (experienced riders). In the summer bathing season, kites only through the Arbousiers channel and only after 19:00 (State boating guide, town order).

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — Arcachon basin cluster

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – La Hume
notes: Shallow tidal basin, ride 3 h either side of high tide; launch through the marked channel at La Hume harbour. Watch the hunting hides on the right and oyster shells. Treated as closed in the hunting season (October–November, town order).

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local ocean beach

name: La Teste – La Salie
notes: Ocean beach south of the Pyla dune, waves. From 25 June to 5 September kites launch only in the 100 m kite zone 100 m north of the La Salie Nord bathing area (or at La Lagune), flagged daily; keep 50 m from the Wharf at La Salie Sud (La Teste order 2019-358).

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — same lake as Navarrosse

name: Lac de Sanguinet – Port de l'Estey
notes: Flat, shallow water; kiting allowed from the harbour all year (lake rules). Tiny launch: the local school takes riders by boat to a sandbank mid-lake. Rocky lumps (alios) on the bottom.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Landes ocean beach

name: Biscarrosse-Plage
notes: Waves and shorebreak, intermediate to expert riders. Plage Sud: in summer use the kite zone outside the bathing area; never go south of the wooden stakes (military test range).

country: # archived: WHE-108 (3 Nov) — only one spot guide mentions kiting here; no school
name: kite zone or Windy kite marker
Contis
notes: Watch the jetties near the river mouth.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local Landes ocean beach

name: Moliets
notes: Beach break with waves; works SW through W to N (the summer N thermal is often stronger here than further south). Best at high tide, with a large area towards the Huchet river mouth.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — local wave spot

name: Seignosse – Les Estagnots
notes: Waves, strong side current and rips, experienced riders. The only Seignosse beach where kiting is allowed; in season use the signposted kite area left (south) of the lifeguarded zone. Summer N–NW thermal is light (10–18 kn). Kite school on the beach.

name: Hossegor – Plage Sud
notes: Plage Sud (Point d'Or); Sud Landes Kite school runs courses from here (Hossegor tourist office). Waves and current, experienced riders. Guides advise against kiting in summer during the lifeguarded hours: check the town orders before riding in July–August. Also: Les Estagnots (Seignosse) 2 km south.

country: # pro: restricted (club / permit / summer ban) — banned in July–August; Anglet kept

name: Hendaye
notes: Long, gently sloping sandy beach facing north, the only Basque beach without cliffs; rocks at the west end at low tide. No kiting 1 July–31 August.

country: # archived: restricted (club / permit / summer ban) — club-only lake

name: Lac d'Orient – Mesnil-Saint-Père
notes: Experienced riders, March to October, through the local clubs (AWA, Flysurf10); beaches closed 15 June–15 September.

country: # archived: restricted (club / permit / summer ban) — club-only lake

name: Lac de Madine
notes: Club-only (AKL membership and FFVL licence required); main beach for SW–W winds, gusty.

name: Île de Ré – La Couarde (Peu Ragot)
notes: Windiest beach of the island in summer thermal wind; a kite zone is listed on the beach and a kite school works from La Couarde (Boutillon). Lifeguarded 11:00-19:00 in July and August: check the town hall for the kite corridor.

name: Île de Ré – Le Gros Jonc
notes: Big beach at Le Bois-Plage with a stretch kept for gliding sports next to the bathing area; named by island guides as a kite spot. Works best at high tide on sand. No kite school confirmed: check locally.

name: Fouras – Plage Nord
notes: Tourist office says kitesurfing is possible on the north beach; watch the rocks at low tide. No school on the beach (nearest at Châtelaillon).

name: Boulogne-sur-Mer
notes: Advanced level, exposed to SW to W winds. Schools such as APG run sessions in the bay of Boulogne depending on wind and tide. Boat traffic from the port: check the rules of the port.

name: Sainte-Cécile
notes: Beach between Le Touquet and Hardelot, promoted by the Camiers – Sainte-Cécile tourist office as a gliding spot for experienced riders. Big tide range, groynes make chop. Kitecamp62 uses it when Stella is too rough.

name: Stella-Plage
notes: Exposed to SW to NW winds from the Channel; often ridden with Merlimont Plage. Kitecamp62 school is based here.

country: # pro: local / secondary beach — added 4 Nov from Windy markers (WHE-108); council kite zone
region: wild beach with a strong current

name: Tarnos – Plage du Métro
notes: Long wild sandy beach north of the Adour jetty, an onshore summer thermal spot (afternoons, best from the north). Part of the beach is set aside for kiters; strong current, intermediate riders. Plage de la Digue, 1.5 km south, is listed as a kite zone too.

country: # pro: restricted (club / permit / summer ban) — added 4 Nov from Windy markers (WHE-108); kiting only off-season in a reserved zone

name: Saint-Jean-de-Luz
notes: Sheltered town bay beach. Kiting only off-season in a reserved zone and never during lifeguard hours, so no kiting here in summer (worst case: dates assumed, check the town's posted order). Surf schools in town also teach kite.
